texts.hotspot_desk_paper: Sheet of paper on the desk
texts.say_villa_first_look: Ashgrove Villa. No lights, no car in the drive. Somebody left in a hurry. Or never left at all.
texts.say_door_unlocked: The key turns like it has been waiting for me. Open.
texts.say_statue_body: Marble, cold and patient. She has watched this garden longer than anyone alive.
texts.say_statue_key_found: A brass key, hooked behind her ear. People hide things where nobody thinks to look up.
texts.say_hall_letter_taken: A letter, left out in the open. Careless. Or meant to be found.
texts.say_pill_bottle_taken: A pill bottle, half empty, the label torn off. Somebody in town will know whose it was.
texts.say_market_first_look: The market square. Two lit windows in the whole town, and both of them are watching me.
texts.say_pills_owner_known: He looked at that bottle a second too long. He knows exactly whose it is.
texts.say_stories_do_not_match: Empty since spring, says one. Coffee every Friday, says the other. One of them is lying to me.
texts.item_brass_key_description: Old and heavy, worn smooth by years of use. It was hidden on the garden statue.
texts.item_pill_bottle_description: Brown glass, a torn label, a dozen white pills. It stood on the desk in the villa hall.
texts.note_hall_letter_body:
You were told what would happen if you kept the ledger.

Midnight. Come alone, and leave the door on the latch.

There is no signature. The ink is still sharp.
texts.note_person_pharmacist_body: Runs the pharmacy on the market square. Chooses every word before he lets it go.
texts.note_person_pharmacist_knows_villa: Says Ashgrove Villa has stood empty since spring.
texts.note_person_pharmacist_pills_prescribed: Made up the sleeping powder himself, three weeks ago, for the housekeeper at Ashgrove.
texts.note_person_cafe_owner_body: Keeps the café on the market square. Sees who comes and who goes.
texts.note_person_cafe_owner_knows_villa: Carried coffee up to the villa every Friday, until last week.
texts.note_person_cafe_owner_recognised_paper: Says the unsigned letter is written on the pharmacy's wrapping paper.
texts.note_obs_stories_do_not_match_body:
The pharmacist says Ashgrove Villa has stood empty since spring. The café owner carried coffee up there every Friday until last week.

Both cannot be true.
texts.dlg_pharmacist_hello: We're closed. ...But you are not here for aspirin, are you.
texts.dlg_pharmacist_no_reaction: I couldn't tell you anything about that.
texts.dlg_pharmacist_villa_1: The Ashgrove place? Nobody has lived up there since spring.
texts.dlg_pharmacist_villa_2: The lights have been out for months. Ask anyone in town.
texts.dlg_pharmacist_night_1: I closed at six and went home. Like every night.
texts.dlg_pharmacist_pills_1: Brown glass, no label... Half the town takes something like that.
texts.dlg_pharmacist_pills_2: Leave it with me, if you like. I could look in my book.
texts.dlg_pharmacist_give_pills_1: ...This is my hand on the label. What is left of it.
texts.dlg_pharmacist_give_pills_2: Sleeping powder. I made it up three weeks ago, for the housekeeper at Ashgrove.
texts.dlg_cafe_owner_hello: Kitchen's closed and the coffee's cold. Sit, if you like.
texts.dlg_cafe_owner_again: Still here? The coffee is still cold.
texts.dlg_cafe_owner_villa_1: Empty? I carried a tray up there every Friday. Until last week.
texts.dlg_cafe_owner_villa_2: Somebody up there likes the coffee strong. And likes it kept quiet.
texts.dlg_cafe_owner_pharmacist_1: He shuts early these days. Keeps the blinds down, too.
texts.dlg_cafe_owner_letter_1: Let me see. ...That is shop paper. The pharmacy wraps its powders in it.
texts.dlg_cafe_owner_letter_2: I would know that blue edge anywhere.
texts.inspection_statue_plaque_text: "Faith and silence." A family motto, cut deep into the brass. Somebody here valued the second word more.
